product_from_film: Moving Image Archive offers a searchable library of historical film clips presented as free to use.
explains_well: One sunset search becomes a selected clip, and the archive samples show a broad human range.
unclear: Download steps and the basis for each clip’s usage rights are not demonstrated.
scenario: Search for historical sunset footage, select a clip and reuse it in a new video.
product_clear_basis: The 120,000 free historical clips statement at 12s is followed by search, results and a selected sunset at 13–15s.

scenes.action: Decorative archive title overlays a presenter and projector. Handwritten yellow words introduce forgetting and remembering; historical-looking clips become a grid under 120,000.
scenes.design: Ornate cream title, yellow handwritten lettering, rounded film edges.
scenes.purpose: Frame the archive as preservation and establish scale.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 0–13s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: A search field receives sun-related text; result thumbnails appear. A sunset is selected with year and duration, shrinks to a small card, then fills the frame.
scenes.design: Black workspace and colored sunset with worn film texture.
scenes.purpose: Demonstrate discovery and reuse through one recognizable image.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 13–21s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Cat, street life, rocket launch, people and an early monochrome man appear with small clip labels and bottom captions.
scenes.design: Varied monochrome and faded color footage, grain and scratches.
scenes.purpose: Show range from ordinary moments to history; captions state early dates and public-domain status.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 21–33s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: The presenter returns in a purple-lit room. Space, city and animation clips alternate with her as captions describe making the tool for friends seeking footage.
scenes.design: Home-like setting, projected ceiling color, old film frames.
scenes.purpose: Give the archive a personal origin.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 33–47s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: Cat, child, sunset and people waving or smiling accompany captions about fragile moments and remembering. Presenter inserts connect the examples.
scenes.design: Longer human and everyday-life shots within soft film borders.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 47–63s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

scenes.action: The archive mark appears on white, with a cat image inserted into its layout. More clips and presenter follow; projector light returns, then a film-style THE END card.
scenes.design: Cream/black typography, projector beam and blue worn end card.
scenes.purpose: Invite exploration and close the film motif.
scenes.evidence: 1 fps source samples in 63–76.868s; state changes visible, exact transition timing/easing unverified.

categories.finding: Preserving memory leads to library scale, a sunset search, collection examples and a personal reason for building the archive.
The title sits over a person/projector image, then Say appears in yellow at 1s. Archive identity is visible but the search task comes later.
The library and free historical clips are stated by 12s; search and selection make the use clear at 15s. Video makers are implied by later captions.
The selected sunset changes from card to full frame; other sections rely on successive clips, presenter framing and text reveals. Exact interpolation is unknown.
A persistent film border and yellow caption color connect different eras. The search-result sunset reappears full frame, maintaining object continuity.
Rounded dark borders, grain, scratches and faded colors suit the archive subject; some may belong to source clips and some may be added.
Large yellow 120,000 establishes scale; small bottom captions carry much of the story. Clip titles/dates are smaller provenance cues.
The inspected ASR draft provides partial script-role support; recognition limits are recorded in A02. Audible voice characteristics and delivery remain unchecked.
categories.reason: Local draft text was read; no direct listening.

categories.finding: Music character and structure are unverified.
Effects and their sources are unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening; waveform peaks do not identify effects.

categories.finding: Sound sync is unverified.
categories.reason: No validated listening or paired audiovisual timing.

categories.finding: Historical-looking scenes and a present-day presenter are visibly mixed. Public-domain status is a film claim; licenses and source records were not checked.
Source duration 76.868 s; Watch metadata 3840 × 2160. Frame rate, audio clipping and export quality not checked here.
categories.reason: Parent source metadata supports duration and dimensions; visual review is sampled.

categories.finding: Search and selection work silently. Many story details remain in small captions, so silent comprehension depends on being able to read them.
The yellow number and central sunset guide the early eye path. Later, meaningful action and bottom captions split attention.
The search is brief but concrete. The long preservation section gives emotional space, while leaving little detail on practical downloading.
categories.experiment: Add one clear download/output state after the sunset selection.

categories.finding: The forgetting/remembering idea is answered by human archival moments and the return to the projector. The practical search promise also receives a small demo.
Everyday cats, children and smiling people beside preservation captions suggest tenderness and concern for memory. Viewer response was not measured.
categories.reason: Emotion inferred from visible material and captions.

categories.finding: The sunset, cat and projector recur, linking the UI, archive examples and presenter into one visual story.
A search and selected clip are shown. Library size, historic dates and reuse permission are stated rather than independently verified.
Ornate archive lettering, handwritten yellow copy and old-film borders strongly match a historical collection.
Search provides useful product proof; the personal explanation gives purpose. A download example would clarify the final user step.
For Tin asset selection, show a search, chosen source and finished use of that exact image, retaining a visible source credit.
categories.experiment: Use one licensed campaign image from query through selected card to published preview.

categories.finding: No human new-viewer test was performed.
categories.reason: The product summary is this model’s film-only reading.

categories.finding: Mobile preview and accessibility checks were not performed.
categories.reason: Contact sheets are evidence views, not a stated mobile preview or compliance test.

lessons.keep: Reuse the exact selected sunset as the full-frame example, so a search visibly leads somewhere.
try: For Tin, search for one campaign asset, select it and show the same image in a finished post with its source visible.
For a creator story, interleave one personal reason with three relevant output examples and keep captions large enough for a separately tested phone view.
lessons.avoid: Letting the preservation story hide the last practical step of obtaining the asset.
lessons.open: Usage rights, library size, dates, voice delivery, music and exact motion remain unverified.

comparison.story: Memory hook → library/search demo → varied historical clips → creator motivation → memory payoff.
comparison.motion: Card scale changes and text reveals; mostly clip-driven sequence, precise transitions unresolved.
comparison.sound: No validated listening; on-screen captions were read as visual text.
comparison.texture: Film borders, scratches, faded color and purple-lit presenter; provenance of effects unknown.
comparison.lesson: A recurring selected clip links product utility to an emotional story.

scope: sampled visual and story review; ASR and measured signal support; no validated audio listening

sound.detail: No validated audio listening. Voice delivery, music, effects and mix are unknown.
sound.evidence: No actual audio perception in this review; prepared audio files are not listening evidence.

sound.detail: The draft supports the preservation story: a searchable library of historical clips, difficulty finding archive footage and keeping recorded moments remembered. Library size, dates and public-domain status remain presenter claims; the archive name is misrecognized. No validated listening; delivery, music, effects, mix and synchronization remain unknown.
sound.visual_relation: Whole-film script role only; ASR timing and audible delivery not validated.
